jobs.title: Program Manager, Housing Services - TRL
jobs.description:
Do you know you have the power to change the course of someone’s life?

Avivo employees do this every day, and we want you to join the team.

At Avivo, our employees work with utter commitment to their clients, embracing the full person, believing in the dignity of all people. We view housing as a human right and recovery as possible for everyone. If you are called to lead with compassion, clarity, and accountability, this role offers a meaningful opportunity to make lasting impact.

Why This Role Matters

The Program Manager, Housing Services
provides leadership for Avivo’s Transitional Recovery Lodging (TRL)
program—an essential bridge for adults and families working toward recovery while participating in Intensive Outpatient Treatment. TRL serves individuals with histories of long‑term homelessness and substance use, offering stability, dignity, and support during a critical moment of change.

This role blends people leadership, program operations, and mission-driven impact, ensuring participants receive high-quality, trauma‑informed services while supporting staff to do their best work.

What You’ll Do

Provide overall leadership and day‑to‑day oversight of Transitional Recovery Lodging, ensuring services are person‑centered, trauma‑informed, recovery‑oriented, and aligned with Housing First and harm‑reduction principles.
Supervise, coach, and develop Program and Client Support Specialists, building a strong, accountable, and supportive team culture.
Ensure 24‑hour program coverage and operational continuity, including participation in an on‑call rotation and providing direct support during urgent situations.
Support participants throughout their stay and during successful transitions upon exit, including planning for housing, employment, education, and community connections.
Develop, implement, and maintain program policies, procedures, and documentation in collaboration with leadership.
Track, analyze, and report program outcomes, compliance requirements, and performance metrics using electronic health records and internal systems.
Manage housing rosters, participant communications related to violations or move‑outs, and Emotional Support Animal (ESA) documentation.
Build and maintain strong relationships with community partners, funders, and internal teams to enhance coordination and participant access to services.
Participate in budgeting, contract monitoring, and funding compliance, communicating risks or changes to leadership.
Actively advance Avivo’s commitment to undoing racism and reducing disparities by leading culturally responsive, inclusive practices and supporting team development in these areas.

Schedule

Full‑time, exempt role with a 32‑hour workweek, supporting strong work‑life balance.
Typically Monday–Friday, daytime hours, with flexibility to meet program needs.
Occasional evenings/weekends and participation in an on‑call rotation may be required.

Qualifications

What You Bring

High school diploma or GED with five years of relevant experience
OR an associate degree in human services or a related field with three years of relevant experience
OR a bachelor's degree in human services or a related field with two years of relevant experience

Minimum of two years of supervisory, leadership, or team lead experience
Experience working in behavioral health, housing, homelessness services, recovery services, or a related field
Experience leading, coaching, and developing staff
Experience with electronic health records and program documentation
Strong knowledge of recovery-oriented services, trauma-informed care, and harm reduction practices
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively in a fast-paced environment
Commitment to culturally responsive and person-centered services
Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel within the community

What We Offer

32-hour full-time work week
Medical Health plan
Health Savings Account (HSA)
Nice Healthcare: offers chat, video visits and in-home primary care visits
Dental plan
Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
Basic Life/AD&D & Voluntary Life/AD&D
Long term disability
Option to purchase critical illness, accident insurance and short-term disability
401(k) Plan
10 Paid holidays & generous PTO

How To Apply

Submit your application online through Avivo’s Careers page at Avivomn.org. Qualified candidates will be contacted for next steps. Early applications encouraged as interviews are conducted on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Telephonic Care Manager (RN) - HCBS Command Team
jobs.description:
Purpose:

Are you an experienced nurse with a background in case management? Are you interested in the opportunity to work from home? UPMC Health Plan is looking for you!

We are hiring a full-time Telephonic Care Manager to join the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Command Team. This position will predominantly work remotely, standard daylight hours, Monday through Friday.

The Telephonic Care Manager is responsible for care coordination and health education for identified Health Plan members through telephonic collaboration with members and their caregivers and providers. Identifies members' medical, behavioral, and social needs and barriers to care. Develops a comprehensive care plan that assists members to close gaps in preventive care, addresses barriers to care, and supports the member's self-management of chronic illness based on clinical standards of care. Collaborates and facilitates care with other medical management staff, other departments, providers, community resources and caregivers to provide additional support. Members are followed by telephone or other electronic communication methods.

Responsibilities:

Present complex members for review by the interdisciplinary team summarizing clinical and social history, healthcare resource utilization, case management interventions.
Update the plan of care following review and communicate recommendations to the member and providers.
Contact members with gaps in preventive health care services and assist them to schedule required screening or diagnostic tests with their providers.
Review member's current medication profile; identify issues related to medication adherence, and address with the member and providers as necessary. Refers member for Comprehensive Medication Review as appropriate.
Conduct comprehensive assessments that include the medical, behavioral, pharmacy, and social needs of the member.
Review UPMC Health Plan data for services the member has received and identify gaps in care based on clinical standards of care.
Refer members to appropriate health plan programs based on assessment data.
Engage members in education or self management programs.
Provide members with appropriate education materials or resources to enhance their knowledge and skills related to physical health, emotional health, or lifestyle management.
Successfully engage member to develop an individualized plan of care in collaboration with their primary care provider that promotes healthy lifestyles, closes gaps in care, and reduces unnecessary ER utilization and hospital readmissions.
Coordinates and modifies the care plan with member, caregivers, PCP, specialists, community resources, behavioral health contractor, and other health plan and system departments as appropriate.
Document all activities in the Health Plan's care management tracking system following Health Plan standards and identify trends and opportunities for improvement based on information obtained from interaction with members and providers.
Conduct member outreach in response to assist with member issues or concerns or facilitate specific population health goals.
Seek input from clinical leadership to resolve issues or concerns.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in a clinical setting and case management nursing required. BSN preferred.
Ability to interact with physicians and other health care professionals in a professional manner required.
Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills required.
Computer proficiency required.
Meet minimum internet system/service and speed/ latency requirements as set forth by UPMC.
Equipment must be connected directly or hard-wired to the internet modem/router with an ethernet cable. Most cable and fiber optic providers can meet the requirement.
Private, secure designated workspace required in the home office setting or the ability to work from a designated UPMC office location daily.

Licensure, Certifications, and Clearances:

Case management certification or approved clinical certification preferred
Registered Nurse (RN)
Act 34
Current licensure either in the state where the facility is located or, if the facility is in a state covered by the multistate Nursing Licensure Compact (NLC) agreement, a multistate license issued by a participating NLC state. Hires and current employees working on an out-of-state NLC license who later change their residency to the state where the facility is also located will have 60 days upon changing their residency to apply for licensure within that state.

UPMC is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Disability/Veteran

jobs.description:
Company Description
Sam Houston State University (SHSU), named for Texas’ renowned statesperson Sam Houston, is committed to academic excellence grounded in a rich historical legacy. Faculty prioritize both student success and advancing knowledge within their disciplines, creating a supportive and engaging learning environment. SHSU serves contemporary learners through traditional on-campus programs and a robust online presence. With more than 20 bachelor’s and graduate degrees offered fully online and additional programs continually in development, SHSU Online is recognized as one of Texas’ leading online education providers. The university emphasizes accessibility, innovation, and student-centered education across all its offerings.
Role Description
Serves as the primary operational liaison between SHSU Online and Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) and is responsible for managing workflows, reporting activities, communications, external partnerships, and operational continuity across multiple functional areas supporting the Distance Education Professional Development Center (DEPDC) initiative. Works collaboratively with technical operations, professional development, instructional support, accessibility, communications, and external partners to ensure DEPDC services operate cohesively, efficiently, and in alignment with statewide grant objectives. Coordinates and participates in meetings with TWC, statewide partners, vendors, Adult Education and Literacy (AEL) providers, and internal stakeholders. Oversees grant deliverables, operational milestones, timelines, compliance requirements, and reporting obligations. Manages collection, organization, and submission of operational reports, participation data, budget-related information, and program documentation. Works collaboratively with SHSU Online operational leaders to ensure alignment, continuity, and effective delivery of DEPDC services. Maintains DEPDC external-facing resources, including websites, social media accounts, communications materials, event resources, and operational documentation. Coordinates with vendors, curriculum providers, and external stakeholders. Monitors public-facing DEPDC information to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and alignment with TWC objectives and SHSU standards. Develops and maintains operational workflows, standard operating procedures (SOPs), transition documentation, and process guides related to DEPDC operations. Identifies opportunities to improve operational efficiency, communication flow, reporting processes, and statewide coordination activities. Assists leadership in evaluating operational effectiveness and implementing continuous improvement efforts. Manages operational activities related to statewide DEPDC webinars, regional trainings, conferences, meetings, and the annual Digital Literacy & Technology Integration Symposium. Performs other related duties as assigned.
Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in education, organizational leadership, project management, communications, public administration, instructional technology, business administration, or related field required. Master’s degree preferred. Eight years of progressively responsible experience in program management, grant administration, project coordination, statewide initiatives, education operations, workforce development, distance learning, adult education, or related areas required. A combination of education, experience, and training that would produce the required knowledge and abilities could be considered.

Purpose:

Are you an experienced nurse with a background in case management? Are you interested in the opportunity to work from home? UPMC Health Plan is looking for you!

We are hiring a full-time Telephonic Care Manager to join the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Command Team. This position will predominantly work remotely, standard daylight hours, Monday through Friday.

The Telephonic Care Manager is responsible for care coordination and health education for identified Health Plan members through telephonic collaboration with members and their caregivers and providers. Identifies members' medical, behavioral, and social needs and barriers to care. Develops a comprehensive care plan that assists members to close gaps in preventive care, addresses barriers to care, and supports the member's self-management of chronic illness based on clinical standards of care. Collaborates and facilitates care with other medical management staff, other departments, providers, community resources and caregivers to provide additional support. Members are followed by telephone or other electronic communication methods.

Responsibilities:

Present complex members for review by the interdisciplinary team summarizing clinical and social history, healthcare resource utilization, case management interventions.
Update the plan of care following review and communicate recommendations to the member and providers.
Contact members with gaps in preventive health care services and assist them to schedule required screening or diagnostic tests with their providers.
Review member's current medication profile; identify issues related to medication adherence, and address with the member and providers as necessary. Refers member for Comprehensive Medication Review as appropriate.
Conduct comprehensive assessments that include the medical, behavioral, pharmacy, and social needs of the member.
Review UPMC Health Plan data for services the member has received and identify gaps in care based on clinical standards of care.
Refer members to appropriate health plan programs based on assessment data.
Engage members in education or self management programs.
Provide members with appropriate education materials or resources to enhance their knowledge and skills related to physical health, emotional health, or lifestyle management.
Successfully engage member to develop an individualized plan of care in collaboration with their primary care provider that promotes healthy lifestyles, closes gaps in care, and reduces unnecessary ER utilization and hospital readmissions.
Coordinates and modifies the care plan with member, caregivers, PCP, specialists, community resources, behavioral health contractor, and other health plan and system departments as appropriate.
Document all activities in the Health Plan's care management tracking system following Health Plan standards and identify trends and opportunities for improvement based on information obtained from interaction with members and providers.
Conduct member outreach in response to assist with member issues or concerns or facilitate specific population health goals.
Seek input from clinical leadership to resolve issues or concerns.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in a clinical setting and case management nursing required. BSN preferred.
Ability to interact with physicians and other health care professionals in a professional manner required.
Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills required.
Computer proficiency required.
Meet minimum internet system/service and speed/ latency requirements as set forth by UPMC.
Equipment must be connected directly or hard-wired to the internet modem/router with an ethernet cable. Most cable and fiber optic providers can meet the requirement.
Private, secure designated workspace required in the home office setting or the ability to work from a designated UPMC office location daily.

Licensure, Certifications, and Clearances:

Case management certification or approved clinical certification preferred
Registered Nurse (RN)
Act 34
Current licensure either in the state where the facility is located or, if the facility is in a state covered by the multistate Nursing Licensure Compact (NLC) agreement, a multistate license issued by a participating NLC state. Hires and current employees working on an out-of-state NLC license who later change their residency to the state where the facility is also located will have 60 days upon changing their residency to apply for licensure within that state.
